PR Summary by Qodo

Add a collapsible desktop sidebar and improve UI contrast ✨ Enhancement 🧪 Tests 🕐 20-40 Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Add localized sidebar labels and persistent collapse controls without a toggle button.
>• Improve text contrast and introduce choice cards for subscription auto-update presets.
>• Give proxy cards more room and test sidebar interactions.
>
Merge Risk 🟡 Medium

Blast radius 🔴 High 💥 6 capabilities

- 6 affected capabilities span independent functional scopes: desktop navigation and sidebar layout, proxy monitoring presentation, subscription management. - The changed labels, navigation buttons, tooltip behavior, width transitions, and page-selection consumer form one bounded end-to-end desktop navigation behavior. - The navigation module consumes the same buttons, so it is a propagation hop rather than an independent capability. - The changed interval cards, selection handler, next-update preview, and subscription save path implement one bounded user outcome: choosing and storing a subscription refresh interval. - The changed grid sizing and retest-button visibility affect how proxy status and its retest action are presented in the proxy page. - They do not alter proxy configuration or core connectivity. - The sidebar consumes shared muted/primary styling and explicit navigation selectors; it is a distinct user-facing navigation presentation within the broader desktop theme. - Subscription controls consume the changed muted/secondary and selected-choice styling; this is a distinct settings outcome from navigation and proxy monitoring. - Proxy status and traffic indicators use the changed contrast overrides, making this an independent visual outcome from the settings and navigation surfaces.
Sources
[apps/desktop/src/styles.css\[1692-1697\]](https://github.com/Juwan-Hwang/Zephyr/blob/bcc81d6b2964bd3c6860c1ebe7f79645a616f399/apps/desktop/src/styles.css#L1692-L1697) ```css available width. Minimum card width 200px, so a long node name and its latency still fit on one row. Unlimited max columns. ============================================ */ #proxies-list { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr)); ``` [apps/desktop/src/main.js\[477-479\]](https://github.com/Juwan-Hwang/Zephyr/blob/bcc81d6b2964bd3c6860c1ebe7f79645a616f399/apps/desktop/src/main.js#L477-L479) ```javascript // Restore the sidebar's expanded/collapsed state before the window is // shown, so it does not jump open once the core has started. registerCleanup(initSidebar()); ``` [apps/desktop/src/ui/settings/subscriptions.js\[666-675\]](https://github.com/Juwan-Hwang/Zephyr/blob/bcc81d6b2964bd3c6860c1ebe7f79645a616f399/apps/desktop/src/ui/settings/subscriptions.js#L666-L675) ```javascript // Auto-update as choice cards: four or more single-choice options use // cards, two or three use a segmented control. const intervalGroup = /** @type {HTMLElement|null} */ (modal.querySelector('#edit-auto-update')); intervalGroup?.style.setProperty('--choice-cols', String(autoUpdateOptions.length)); intervalGroup?.querySelectorAll('.choice-card').forEach((tab) => { tab.addEventListener('click', () => { intervalGroup.querySelectorAll('.choice-card').forEach((b) => { b.setAttribute('aria-checked', b === tab ? 'true' : 'false'); }); intervalGroup.dataset.value = /** @type {HTMLElement} */ (tab).dataset.value || '0'; ```
Behavioral complexity 🔴 High 🧩 Interacting branches, State transitions

- Before: the sidebar was a fixed icon-only navigation layout with existing navigation and tooltip behavior. - After: it has persisted expanded/collapsed state, narrow-window overlay state, drag snapping, keyboard/context-menu toggles, resize transitions, and tooltip suppression/re-enablement. - New correctness conditions are that wide-window persistence must not be overwritten by automatic narrow-window collapse, overlay state must track expansion, drag snapping must agree with the final persisted state, and tooltip visibility must agree with the current label layout. - These are newly interacting UI states, not merely reuse of existing navigation.
Potential damage 🟡 Medium 🩹 Temporary loss

- A bad state transition can temporarily impair access to page navigation or leave the sidebar visually unusable. - Reloading the window or toggling the state can restore the UI; the changed localStorage value is validated and can be replaced. - There is no evidence of persistent backend corruption or external side effects. - Recoverable by reload or another reachable toggle path; if the UI is completely inaccessible, reopening the desktop window is the supported practical recovery. - Reverting code alone does not remove an already saved expanded/collapsed preference, but the preference is limited to this UI.
Sources
[apps/desktop/src/main.js\[477-479\]](https://github.com/Juwan-Hwang/Zephyr/blob/bcc81d6b2964bd3c6860c1ebe7f79645a616f399/apps/desktop/src/main.js#L477-L479) ```javascript // Restore the sidebar's expanded/collapsed state before the window is // shown, so it does not jump open once the core has started. registerCleanup(initSidebar()); ```
Assessed commit bcc81d6
Diagram

```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 direction TD state "Wide expanded" as WideExpanded state "Wide collapsed" as WideCollapsed state "Narrow collapsed" as NarrowCollapsed state "Narrow overlay" as NarrowOverlay WideExpanded --> WideCollapsed: toggle or drag WideCollapsed --> WideExpanded: toggle or drag WideExpanded --> NarrowCollapsed: window narrows WideCollapsed --> NarrowCollapsed: window narrows NarrowCollapsed --> NarrowOverlay: toggle or drag NarrowOverlay --> NarrowCollapsed: dismiss or toggle NarrowCollapsed --> WideExpanded: widen; saved expanded NarrowCollapsed --> WideCollapsed: widen; saved collapsed NarrowOverlay --> WideExpanded: widen; saved expanded NarrowOverlay --> WideCollapsed: widen; saved collapsed ```
High-Level Assessment

>Keep sidebar interaction state in a small frontend controller while retaining the existing navigation and shared context-menu utility. CSS-only responsive collapse would not cover saved preferences, drag snapping, or temporary narrow-window expansion; a native or Rust implementation is unnecessary for these UI behaviors.

Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (0) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📎 Requirement gaps (0) 🎨 UX issues (0) 🔗 Cross-repo conflicts (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Scaled users cannot reliably drag closed ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: bcc81d6

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>onDown now divides the bounding-box width by the UI scale (startW = rect.width / scale) and stores
>scale in the drag state; onMove divides the pointer delta by drag.scale, so the drag width is
>computed in layout CSS pixels before clamping and snapping. This matches the suggested fix's intent
>(convert initial width and pointer delta to CSS pixels using the active UI scale), though it is
>implemented via a stored scale value rather than exactly as described. Also the isNarrow check uses
>uiScale(). Tests were added for UI scaling.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>onDown reads the sidebar’s transformed bounding-box width, then onMove combines it with pointer
>pixels and writes the result as an untransformed CSS width. At the supported 150% UI scale, dragging
>an expanded English sidebar 100 screen pixels toward collapse still computes a width above the snap
>threshold, so it remains expanded.
>
>

2. Scaled windows collapse too late ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: bcc81d6

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>isNarrow now divides window.innerWidth by uiScale() (read from the --ui-scale CSS variable) before
>comparing with NARROW_PX, so scaled windows are treated as narrow at the correct layout width. A
>MutationObserver on the root element's style attribute calls onResize when the UI scale changes, so
>the sidebar is reevaluated on scale changes as well as resizes. Drag handling was also scaled to
>match. Tests cover the 150% case.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>isNarrow compares the unscaled window.innerWidth with 860 even though the body’s usable layout
>width is divided by --ui-scale. At 150% scale, a 900-pixel window has roughly 600 CSS pixels of
>layout width but is treated as wide, so the expanded sidebar still takes space from the content
>instead of using the narrow-window behavior.
>
>
3. Narrow-window drags shift the page ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: bcc81d6

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>onDown now adds the 'sidebar-overlay' class when the window is narrow (isNarrow()), so the sidebar
>overlays the content for the whole drag instead of reflowing the page. The drag width is also kept
>in CSS px via --sidebar-drag-w and the overlay margin CSS was updated to use that variable. This
>addresses the reflow-during-drag problem at drag start rather than synchronizing overlay state in
>onMove on each move, so it differs from the suggested fix but is a valid implementation.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>onMove toggles sidebar-expanded without updating sidebar-overlay or overlayOpen. While
>dragging the sidebar open in a narrow window, its increased width participates in the flex layout
>and pushes the page until pointer release calls apply.
>
>
4. Editor shortcuts toggle the sidebar ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: bcc81d6

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Added shortcutBelongsElsewhere(e), which returns true for defaultPrevented events, targets inside
>input/textarea/select/contenteditable/.cm-editor, or when an aria-modal dialog is open. onKey now
>only calls preventDefault and toggle when isToggleShortcut(e, mac) && !shortcutBelongsElsewhere(e).
>Editable-target events are left alone, so the editor keeps Ctrl+B. The fix is in the same onKey
>handler the finding flagged, and it also adds a unit test for the textarea case.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>onKey handles the sidebar chord at document level without checking whether the event originated in
>an editable control. Pressing Ctrl+B in the app’s text editor reaches this handler and calls
>preventDefault() and toggle(), intercepting the editor’s shortcut while changing navigation.
>
>
View medium (4)
5. Visible sidebar labels keep old tooltips ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: bcc81d6

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Sidebar state changes now dispatch 'zephyr:sidebar-change', and nav-tooltip listens for it and hides
>any visible tooltip. The guard also hides the tooltip when a label is not truncated, so a stale
>tooltip cannot remain next to a fully visible label.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>show checks whether an expanded label is truncated only when it is called, without reconsidering a
>tooltip already on screen when the sidebar changes state. If a collapsed button’s tooltip is visible
>and the user expands the sidebar using the shortcut, that tooltip remains alongside the now-visible
>label until another tooltip event hides it.
>
>
6. Selected cards lose a visible focus ring ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: bcc81d6

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The selected-card focus-visible rule was changed from a 3px 28%-opacity accent halo to a two-layer
>box-shadow: a 2px gap in the elevated background color followed by a 2px solid accent-primary ring
>(0 0 0 2px var(--zephyr-bg-elevated), 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-primary)). This gives a solid,
>high-contrast focus indicator for selected cards in place of the faint translucent halo. It does not
>use the suggested focus-ring token, but it addresses the same issue with a different valid
>implementation.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>The selected choice card’s :focus-visible rule replaces the normal focus ring with a 28%-opacity
>accent halo. When a keyboard user focuses a selected auto-update option, that faint halo is
>difficult to distinguish from the already-tinted selected state, particularly on the light card
>surface.
>
>
7. Sidebar jumps open after the core finishes starting ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: bcc81d6

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The commit moves registerCleanup(initSidebar()) above the core-startup wait in initApp (main.js), so
>the sidebar is initialized and its saved state restored before the core is awaited, with a comment
>stating the goal is to avoid the jump before the window is shown. This matches the suggested option
>of moving the initSidebar call above the startCoreAndConfigure loop, though it does not add a
>separate synchronous applyInitialSidebarState() and the call is still not strictly synchronous
>before the window shows (initSidebar is called before the await of _backendListenersReady in the
>same function's flow, not before the window is displayed). The suggested fix's core idea is
>implemented, so this is judged a match.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>initSidebar() is the only code that adds sidebar-expanded and restores the saved state, and it
>runs in initApp only after await startCoreAndConfigure() (which loops on retry). The window is
>shown 50 ms after launch, so until the core is up the sidebar renders at the CSS default (80 px,
>labels hidden). With the default 'expanded' preference in a wide window it then widens to 160/192 px
>and shoves the whole content area sideways on every launch. Its shortcut, right-click menu and edge
>drag also do nothing while startup is waiting on the core or showing the core-error card.
>
>
8. Light mode shows the red Delete plugin button in blue ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: bcc81d6

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The commit replaces the broad selector .btn-ghost[class] with .btn-ghost.active, so only active
>ghost buttons get the accent blue. The .btn-ghost.text-[var(--text-secondary)] exemption rule is
>removed, so the red Delete button and other ghost buttons no longer get forced blue. This matches
>the suggested recommended fix (scope to .btn-ghost.active), though it does not add the
>#edit-url-change selector or the :not([class*="text-red"]) exclusion.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>The new rule :root:not(.dark) .btn-ghost[class] { color: #0058c2 } has specificity (0,4,0), so it
>beats every single-class colour utility on a ghost button. Only .text-[var(--text-secondary)] is
>exempted. In light mode the plugin 'Delete' action (btn-ghost text-red-400) now shows in accent
>blue, and every other ghost button changes from primary text to blue, including their hover state.
>
>

## What is [CodSpeed](https://codspeed.io)?
CodSpeed is a **continuous benchmarking** platform that allows you to **track** and **compare** the **performance** of your codebase during development.

It uses a smart **runtime engine** to measure the performance of your code in an **accurate** and **reproducible** way without creating a huge **runtime overhead**, unlike traditional benchmarks.

CodSpeed produces detailed **performance reports** helping you **improve** your codebase **performance**, directly **within your repository provider** (Pull Requests comments, Merge checks, ...).

## How it works

The core of the **performance measurement** is done directly within your **CI environment** through the **CodSpeed Action**. Allowing you to **stay the sole owner** of your data and to keep your **codebase private**.

Once the performance data is generated, **only the benchmark results** are sent to the CodSpeed servers to be **analyzed**.

Then, performance reports are **generated** and **published** directly **within your repository provider**.

## How long does it take to install?

If you're **already benchmarking** your codebase, you can plug your **existing benchmarks** to CodSpeed in **less than 5 minutes** since CodSpeed benchmark's API is **compatible** with the most **popular benchmarking frameworks**.

If **you haven't any benchmarks yet**, we provide an **intuitive** benchmarking API that allows you to **create your first benchmarks** in a **few minutes**.
